title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) that measures how often LLM-produced network‑configuration proposals would trigger unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action) and whether an automated defended pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the observed counts were n11=271, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (baseline safe rate 271/272 = 0.9963235; guarded safe rate 272/272 = 1.0). The absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00367647, paired‑bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00000, 0.01102941] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. A verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not execute (execution manifest documents stage_counts and provider‑call audit). All raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs, provider traces, validator traces, and a full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest are archived and referenced in the Disclosure. We report the archived, artifact‑grounded numeric results, describe the verified deviation, present conservative sensitivity accounting for failed provider calls, and discuss operational implications for trustworthy agentic NetOps evaluation.

sections.introduction: LLM‑driven agentic NetOps systems translate operator intent into concrete configuration changes and tool calls. When a fluent textual claim is converted into an action against live network state, the risk surface includes misconfiguration, policy breach, or reachability loss. Prior defenses in the literature include deterministic network validators, generate–validate–repair loops, ensemble/consensus gating, and human‑in‑the‑loop checkpoints. We preregistered a paired experiment to (1) quantify the empirical claim→action rate under an unguarded pipeline and (2) estimate the effect of an automated guarded pipeline on that rate. The preregistration (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; SHA‑256 fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) fixed the estimand (paired difference in safe rates), sampling and missingness rules, validator, and analysis procedures. We executed the frozen plan and archive every artifact (responses, scoring JSONs, provider traces, execution manifest) with recorded SHA‑256 values to enable deterministic verification.
sections.related_work: Deterministic validation and formal verification (NetKAT, header‑space, SMT approaches) provide operationally meaningful correctness checks used in NetOps research and practice; they motivated our deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scorer. Recent LLM‑for‑AIOps and agentic‑NetOps work propose tool augmentation, generate‑validate‑repair workflows, and multimodel consensus to reduce hallucinated actions or unsafe tool calls. Unlike prior descriptive or single‑case reports, this study is preregistered, paired, and artifact‑anchored: every numeric claim is traceable to archived JSON scoring artifacts and provider traces (manifest recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered primary estimand is the paired difference in safe execution rates (safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline) computed on complete pairs. Design, sampling, and analysis were frozen prior to execution: paired binary design, planned N=300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial planned), single automatic retry policy for model calls, McNemar exact two‑sided test for confirmatory inference, and paired‑bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Task generation and simulator. A deterministic task generator produced synthetic intent→configuration tasks with encoded workflow invariants (e.g., must‑be‑down for MTU/VLAN edits, minimum‑up invariants, ordered sequences). Each task includes initial state, required sequence, and a canonical reference. Validator and scoring. We used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 to evaluate the generated configuration against task invariants and to produce a structured validator_trace per episode (parsed command counts, observed touched fields, final simulated state, violation codes). Execution and orchestration. The execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) records orchestration, provider call counts, per‑file SHA‑256s, and stage_counts. The preregistered guarded pipeline specified: deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The actual execution (artifact) is authoritative and is used for all reported numbers. Missingness and sensitivity. Complete pairs were defined per preregistered rules (both baseline and guarded modes produced a parsable binary safe/unsafe outcome). Episodes where provider calls failed after the allowed retry were recorded as failed; primary analysis uses complete pairs only; a preregistered conservative sensitivity treats failed episodes as unsafe on planned N=300.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact values). Planned episodes = 600 (paired design); completed episodes = 544; failed episodes = 56. Provider‑call audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (execution/execution_manifest.json; archived with full SHA‑256 manifest). Complete pairs and primary contingency (artifact values). Complete pairs analyzable = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 682a629a...). Contingency counts (complete pairs N=272): n11 = 271 (safe both baseline and guarded), n10 = 1 (safe baseline, unsafe guarded), n01 = 0 (unsafe baseline, safe guarded), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline safe rate = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded safe rate = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.003676470588235281. Inference and uncertainty (artifact‑computed). Paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.00000, 0.011029411764705883] (analysis log and bootstrap seeds archived). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservative sensitivity (preregistered). Treating the 28 failed provider calls conservatively as unsafe on the planned N=300 yields: baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; absolute difference = 0.0033333333. Representative per‑episode artifacts. Representative scoring JSONs and responses are archived; examples in manuscript bundle include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 465d73fd...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = b227731a...), and their paired response texts (execution/responses/...). Verified orchestration deviation (artifact evidence). The execution manifest documents stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300, "guarded":1} and the provider‑call audit counts above; these fields prove the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not execute. Consequently the archived guarded condition evaluates deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation; the preregistered ensemble hypothesis therefore remains untested in this run. The execution manifest path and full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest are authoritative (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and operational implications. The executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) produced nearly perfect acceptance on analyzable pairs, but the absolute paired improvement over baseline is small and statistically inconclusive on the complete pairs (McNemar p = 1.0). Because the preregistered ensemble stage did not run, no claim regarding multimodel‑consensus effect can be made from this execution. Orchestration reliability lesson: provider call failures (28 failed calls) materially reduced the effective sample and should be mitigated by deterministic caching, stronger retry/backoff policies, and live orchestration checks in future executions. Validator usefulness and auditability: deterministic validators yield machine‑readable traces that support reproducible per‑episode adjudication and post‑hoc failure analysis (see the archived validator_trace fields inside execution/scoring/*.json). Threats to validity. Internal validity: single declared model in the executed archive (gpt-5-mini) — no multi‑model generality; prompt sensitivity and generation nondeterminism are a concern (we recorded seeds and cached responses where applicable). Construct validity: synthetic tasks and simulator may not capture full vendor behavior or operational complexity; validator abstraction choices (the operational invariants encoded) determine what is called 'unsafe'. External validity: synthetic task bank size and simulator restrict generalization; operational deployment would include telemetry, operator overrides, and richer topologies. Conclusion validity: effective N was reduced by provider‑call failures (28), lowering power for small absolute effects; the observed paired difference is therefore uncertain. Missing preregistered item and artifact path. The peer review requested realized prompt‑family counts (benign/ambiguous/adversarial) for (a) the planned N=300 tasks, (b) the analyzable complete pairs N=272, and (c) the 28 failed episodes. That breakdown is deterministically derivable from the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl; the canonical artifact path and SHA‑256 are execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3d7b63c361c9848b20750cc44125f195f0341346d48393ce72ae07d6c0fea745). The supplied high‑level analysis summaries included in this manuscript bundle do not contain the precomputed per‑family counts; therefore we cannot truthfully enumerate the per‑family counts here without re‑parsing execution/task_manifest.jsonl. The file is archived with the manifest above and allows deterministic reconstruction; the omission is procedural (a missing per‑family summary in the analysis outputs) not a data fabrication. Reproducibility note. Minimal artifacts to reproduce the primary contingency are archived and SHA‑256s are provided in the Disclosure. Follow‑up re‑execution recommendation. To test the preregistered ensemble hypothesis, re‑run the protocol under hardened orchestration (deterministic caching, robust retries, and run‑time monitors) so that the ensemble stage executes and stage_counts in execution manifest match the preregistration. This run provides an artifact‑grounded lesson: validators plus gates can be effective, but orchestration must be engineered and audited to evaluate ensemble effects.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired, artifact‑anchored evaluation of claim→action risk in agentic NetOps pipelines. The archived run (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1) yielded 272 analyzable pairs with near‑perfect guarded acceptance under the executed pipeline (validator + human gate on a single generation), but the preregistered multimodel ensemble stage did not run due to a verified orchestration deviation. All raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs, provider traces, validator traces, and a full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest are archived for deterministic verification. The principal scientific conclusion is therefore bounded: deterministic validators provide auditable, reproducible adjudication and can reduce unsafe executions when combined with gating in this simulated setting, but the preregistered ensemble question remains unanswered and requires re‑execution under improved orchestration. Detailed artifacts and hashes are provided to enable independent verification and re‑runs.

limitations: Single declared model present in the archived execution (declared model = "gpt-5-mini"); no multi‑model generality claims are supported by this run.
Synthetic tasks and a deterministic simulator were used; construct and external validity versus vendor hardware and production topologies are limited.

A verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a different pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation).
Provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced the effective sample and limited power to detect small absolute effects.
